**Synopsis:**
On Aug 31, 2026, US equity futures fell as US-Iran military strikes disrupted Strait of Hormuz oil flows, spiking Brent crude ~1.71% and reigniting inflation fears. Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole debut the prior Friday cemented expectations of a September rate hike (>60% probability per CME FedWatch, up sharply from 41.4% a week prior). All S&P 500 sectors except Energy sold off. PG&E cratered 18% on wildfire liability exposure. Semis and AI-linked names (Nvidia, Intel, TXN) outperformed. September 4 jobs report is the next key catalyst.

---

**Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US stock market pricing?**
Relevance: YES — Directly covers Fed rate hike expectations, inflation dynamics, and live US equity market moves across all major indices (SPX, NDX, DJIA).

---

**Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?**
Risk score: **72 / 100**
> The US-Iran military escalation and Strait of Hormuz disruption is a **new, high-uncertainty geopolitical shock**. Warsh's hawkishness amplifies an already-shifting rate narrative. The combination of a hot PCE, a new hawkish Fed Chair, and active military conflict driving oil prices creates a risk cocktail that markets had not fully priced just a week prior (41% → 60%+ hike odds). This is materially new forward risk, not stale information.

---

**Q03. Is the content explicitly about bullish impact on the US stock markets?**
Explicit: NO
Impact score: **12 / 100**
> Only narrow pockets of bullishness: Energy stocks, select semis (Nvidia, Intel, TXN), and GameStop. These are isolated, sector-specific moves — not a broad bullish signal.

---

**Q04. Is the content explicitly about bearish impact on the US stock markets?**
Explicit: YES
Impact score: **68 / 100**
> Broad market selloff across SPX, NDX, DJIA. Rate hike odds surging, oil-driven inflation fears, geopolitical escalation, a hawkish Fed Chair removing cut optionality, and September seasonality all align bearishly. PG&E's 18% single-stock collapse adds idiosyncratic downside weight. Forward risk skew is clearly to the downside into the Sept 4 jobs report and Sept FOMC.
